newsitem.title: EGYPT: Rights group wants Egypt inmates in Israel released.
newsitem.headline: Rights group wants Egypt inmates in Israel released.

text.p: An Egyptian rights group said on Wednesday Israel was mistreating Egyptian prisoners and urged President Hosni Mubarak to intervene to secure their release.
The independent Egyptian Human Rights Organisation for Human Rights (EOHR) also said Israel refused to release several Egyptian inmates whose jail terms had long expired.

A statement by the rights group highlighted the case of Mahmoud Suleiman el-Sawarkah, 67. It said he was in poor health and began a hunger strike on Tuesday to protest against his detention at Ashkelon prison.
Sawarkah is serving a 450-year sentence for throwing a grenade at an Israeli military patrol in 1977, killing a soldier and wounding five others, EOHR said.
The group said it had learned the Israeli government had turned down a request by Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa for Sawarkah's release because he was a security prisoner.
EOHR said Sawarkah was on the verge of death. "Medical students carried out four unsuccessful operations on his stomach. The Israeli authorities have treated him as a guinea pig," it added.
"He now complains of extreme stomach enlargement and extremely poor eyesight. Ashkelon prison administrators will not let his family in to visit him," it added.
The group listed eight Egyptian prisoners who are being held in Ashkelon and two other prisons along with other Egyptians whose jail terms had expired.
"They live under tragic conditions in these prisons and are denied all their human rights guaranteed by international and humanitarian conventions and norms," EOHR said.
"EOHR urges the president of the republic to personally intervene to secure the release of all Egyptian prisoners in Israeli jails," it added.
